title: Regression: Routes still advertised to T3 from UT2 in TSA mode with `CONFED` BGP config
author: arista-nwolfe
body:
### Is it platform specific

Specific to UT2 topology

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Previous Working Version

202511

### Steps to Reproduce

Executes `TSA` on a UT2 device with CONFED BGP config and note that the UT2 stops advertising routes to the LT2 but still advertises routes to the T3:
```
>  show ip bgp summary
Neighbhor      V     AS    MsgRcvd    MsgSent    TblVer    InQ    OutQ  Up/Down      State/PfxRcd  NeighborName
-----------  ---  -----  ---------  ---------  --------  -----  ------  ---------  --------------  --------------
10.0.0.1       4  65200       7374       6679    306965      0       0  00:13:25            34050  VM01T3
10.0.0.3       4  65200       7386       6721    306965      0       0  00:13:22            34050  VM02T3
10.0.0.5       4  65200       7384       6702    306965      0       0  00:13:20            34050  VM03T3
10.0.0.101     4  65300       6938       7331    306965      0       0  04:54:35              257  VM05LT2
10.0.0.103     4  65300       6947       7331    306965      0       0  04:54:35              257  VM07LT2
```
```
# TSC no-stats
System Mode: Maintenance
```
```
root@ctn104:~# show ip bgp neighbors 10.0.0.101 advertised-routes | tail -n 5

     Network          Next Hop            Metric LocPrf Weight Path
*>  10.1.0.1/32      0.0.0.0                  0    100  32768 i

Total number of prefixes 1, total number of paths 1
root@ctn104:~# show ip bgp neighbors 10.0.0.103 advertised-routes | tail -n 5

     Network          Next Hop            Metric LocPrf Weight Path
*>  10.1.0.1/32      0.0.0.0                  0    100  32768 i

Total number of prefixes 1, total number of paths 1
root@ctn104:~# show ip bgp neighbors 10.0.0.1 advertised-routes | tail -n 5
*>  194.55.243.0/25  0.0.0.0                                0 65200 64999 65900 i
*>  194.55.243.128/25
                    0.0.0.0                                0 65200 64999 65900 i

Total number of prefixes 51207, total number of paths 51207
```

The issue is evident when looking at the `vtysh -c "show run"`, the LT2 neighbors are in the peer-group `PEER_V4` while the T3 neighbors aren't:
```
router bgp 66000
neighbor 10.0.0.101 remote-as 65300
neighbor 10.0.0.101 peer-group PEER_V4   <----- MISSING on T3
neighbor 10.0.0.101 description VM05LT2
neighbor 10.0.0.101 timers 3 10
neighbor 10.0.0.101 timers connect 10

neighbor 10.0.0.1 remote-as 65200
neighbor 10.0.0.1 description VM01T3
neighbor 10.0.0.1 timers 3 10
neighbor 10.0.0.1 timers connect 10 
```

When I try to add the T3 neighbor into this peer group it gets rejected:
```
# config
(config)# router bgp 66000
(config-router)# neighbor 10.0.0.1 peer-group PEER_V4
% Peer-group members must be all internal or all external.
```

It appears the issue is in CONFED BGP the LT2 neighbors are treated as `internal` while the T3 neighbors are treated as `external` and they aren't allowed to share a peer-group.

### Impact of this regression

TSA is broken on UT2

```

```

linkedPullRequests.title: [bgpcfgd] Fix TSA route leak to confed-external peers in CONFED BGP
linkedPullRequests.author: YatishSVC
linkedPullRequests.body:
### Why I did it
On BGP-confederation devices (e.g. UT2 ), FRR classifies neighbors by ASN relative to the local confederation:
- **confed-internal** = the local member ASN (iBGP) **and** the configured confederation peers (e.g. LT2) → treated as *internal*
- **confed-external** = everything else (e.g. T3) → treated as *external*

The `general` FRR templates place **every** neighbor into `PEER_V4`/`PEER_V6`. FRR refuses to mix internal and external members in one peer-group (`Peer-group members must be all internal or all external`), so the confed-external (T3) neighbors end up with **no peer-group at all**, and therefore **no outbound route-map**.

TSA works by rewriting the peer-group's `out` route-map (`TO_BGP_PEER_V4/V6`). Since the T3 neighbors have no peer-group / out route-map, **TSA cannot stop advertising routes to them → routes leak to T3 during TSA** on confed devices.

Fixes #28551

### Relationship to #28516
#28516 added a guard so `DeviceGlobalCfgMgr` skips the `CONFED` key (preventing the spurious TSB in #28515). This PR covers that **same** `DeviceGlobalCfgMgr` code path **and** the FRR peer-group/template fix, so **#28516 is being closed in favour of this PR**.

This PR carries the guard itself, in the fail-closed **allowlist** form (`if key != "STATE": return True`) that the **internal branch already uses** — so it *converges* the public/internal divergence in `managers_device_global.py` instead of adding a competing guard. `CONFED` is stored in the bgpcfgd `Directory` **inside** that guard (and removed on delete) so the peer templates can read the confederation asn/peers, while the TSA/W-ECMP/IDF handlers are never run on a CONFED update.

### How I did it
- Add a second peer-group `PEER_EXTERNAL_V4`/`PEER_EXTERNAL_V6`, rendered **only when a confederation is configured**, that reuses the **same** in/out route-maps (`FROM_BGP_PEER_V4` / `TO_BGP_PEER_V4` …) as `PEER_V4`.
- In `instance.conf.j2`, assign a neighbor to `PEER_EXTERNAL_*` when it is confed-external (ASN ≠ local member ASN **and** not in the confederation `peers` list); otherwise keep `PEER_V4/V6`.
- `DeviceGlobalCfgMgr.set_handler` stores the `BGP_DEVICE_GLOBAL|CONFED` row in the bgpcfgd `Directory` (and `del_handler` removes it), and returns early so the TSA/W-ECMP/IDF handlers are not run on a CONFED update. `bgpcfgd` passes `CONFIG_DB__BGP_DEVICE_GLOBAL` to the peer templates so they can read the confederation asn/peers.
- Register `PEER_EXTERNAL_V4/V6` under `bgp.peers.general.bbr` in `constants.yml.j2` so BBR toggles `allowas-in` on them exactly like `PEER_V4/V6` (no-op on non-confed devices, where those peer-groups are absent from the running config).

**No TSA change is needed:** because `PEER_EXTERNAL_*` reuses `TO_BGP_PEER_V4/V6 out`, the existing TSA logic (which rewrites that route-map) automatically covers the external peer-group too.

**No regression on non-confed devices:** the whole `PEER_EXTERNAL` block is guarded by `CONFIG_DB__BGP_DEVICE_GLOBAL is defined and 'CONFED' in …`. When there is no confederation (or the row is absent) the templates render **byte-identically** to today (everything stays in `PEER_V4/V6`).

### Validation done in this PR
- [x] Rendered `peer-group.conf.j2` + `instance.conf.j2` for a confed device: T3 (AS 65200) → `PEER_EXTERNAL_V4`, LT2 (confed peer AS 65300) → `PEER_V4`, iBGP (AS 66000) → `PEER_V4`; `PEER_EXTERNAL_V4` reuses `TO_BGP_PEER_V4 out`.
- [x] Confed data path: verified `set_handler` stores `CONFED` so `get_slot` exposes it to the template (previously the fix would have been a silent no-op); `del_handler` removes it.
- [x] All 6 existing non-confed `peer-group.conf` golden cases render with **no** `PEER_EXTERNAL` → existing template unit tests unaffected.
- [x] **bgpcfgd unit tests added:** `general/instance.conf` confed fixtures (confed-external T3 → `PEER_EXTERNAL_V4/V6`; confed-internal peer AS in `peers` → `PEER_V4`) and a negative-key regression `test_set_handler_unknown_key_does_not_run_tsa` (an unknown key must not reach `configure_tsa()`, guarding #28515). `test_device_global` 22/22 and `test_templates`+`test_bbr` 69/69 pass.

### Still to do (tracked)
- [x] Add bgpcfgd unit-test cases (`tests/data/general/instance.conf/param_confed*` + golden, and `DeviceGlobalCfgMgr` handler tests) — done in this PR.
- [ ] Live TSA validation on a confed UT2 box running the public `general` templates: after `TSA`, confirm advertised-routes to T3 == 0.

### Description for the changelog
Fix TSA route leak to confed-external peers on BGP confederation devices by giving them a dedicated peer-group that shares the TSA-managed out route-map.

#### Which release branch to backport (provide reason below if selected)
- [x] 202511
- [x] 202605

#### How did you verify/test it?
- bgpcfgd unit tests (run on `master`): `test_device_global` 24/24 and `test_templates` 18/18, including the new confed `instance.conf`/`peer-group.conf` fixtures, the `prime_confed_from_config_db` success + None-table tests, and the negative-key regression for #28515.
- Template render for a confed device confirms confed-external (T3, AS 65200) → `PEER_EXTERNAL_V4/V6` reusing the TSA-managed `TO_BGP_PEER_V4/V6 out`, while confed-internal peers stay in `PEER_V4/V6`; non-confed devices render byte-identically (no `PEER_EXTERNAL`).
- **202511 / 202605:** the bgpcfgd + FRR-template code path is identical on both branches (the allowlist guard already exists there), so the same unit tests apply.
- **Live on-hardware TSA validation is still pending** (tracked in *Still to do*): it needs a confed device on the public `general` templates; our lab confed boxes run the internal `msft.general` set.
